title: Flutter 3.38.1: Failed to Verify when Submitting to App Store Connect
body: After upgrading to Flutter 3.38.1, validating my iOS archive fails with: "The binary is invalid. The encryption info in the LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO load command is either missing or invalid, or the binary is already encrypted. This binary does not seem to have been built with Apple's linker." This did not happen before the upgrade. My environment is macOS 15.6.1, Xcode 16.3, and Flutter stable 3.38.1; flutter doctor reports no issues.

symptoms_visible: App Store Connect rejects my iOS archive after upgrading to Flutter 3.38.1, saying the LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO data is missing or invalid and the binary does not seem to have been built with Apple's linker.
N0.label: N0 archive validation failure reported

symptoms_visible: The same archive-validation error still prevents me from submitting the app.
N1.label: N1 project dependencies collected

symptoms_visible: After updating to Flutter 3.38.2 and running flutter clean, distributing the archive still produces the same LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO validation error.
N2_x.label: N2_x update and clean aftermath

symptoms_visible: Xcode's Validate App action fails with the same invalid-binary and LC_ENCRYPTION_INFO message, so the problem is not limited to Distribute App.
N3.label: N3 validation path and project files checked

symptoms_visible: After running flutter clean and flutter build ios --config-only before archiving, the archive validates successfully as long as I do not run flutter run first.
N4.label: N4 pre-archive workaround verified

symptoms_visible: My archive validates when I use the clean pre-archive procedure; maintainers report that the corresponding Flutter tooling fix is available, but I did not report retesting that fixed SDK on my own project.
N_terminal.label: terminal workaround confirmed and tooling fix available

question_patterns: Can you share your pubspec.yaml so we can see which packages and overrides are in the affected app?
Which dependencies does this project use?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Here is my pubspec.yaml. Among the dependencies it includes sqflite_sqlcipher 3.4.0, and dependency_overrides includes sqlite3 3.0.1, along with the rest of my application packages.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: This is a newly created counter app with no third-party dependencies or dependency overrides.
The app uses the same sqlite-related dependencies, but the unrelated UI packages have slightly newer versions.

edges.comment: Reporter c1 supplied the requested pubspec. This edge describes only the opening reporter's project; later counter-app reports are a separate non-native-assets manifestation and are not merged into this causal chain.

solution.intent: Treat the failure as a transient Flutter-version or stale-build problem and retry after updating Flutter and running flutter clean.
solution.concrete_example: Update from Flutter 3.38.1 to 3.38.2, run flutter clean, rebuild the archive, and submit it again.

edges.comment: Reporter c9: the reporter installed Flutter 3.38.2 and ran flutter clean, but the identical validation error remained. The installed Flutter version is a persistent system change, so the aftermath uses S1b.

question_patterns: Does the same error occur if you choose Validate App instead of Distribute App?
Can you run Xcode's validation action separately and report what happens?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes. I tried Validate App separately and still got the same errors.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Validate App succeeds; the error occurs only during the Distribute App upload step.
Validate App shows the same error but with a different generated ID.

question_patterns: Can you provide Info.plist, Runner.xcodeproj, and pubspec.lock for the affected project?
Please share the requested iOS project and lock files so the build can be reproduced.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I've attached the requested Info.plist, Runner.xcodeproj, and pubspec.lock together in sup-files.zip.

edges.comment: Reporter c12-c14: the original reporter confirmed the failure occurs during Validate App and supplied the requested project files. The screenshot from c14 is attached to the validation answer.

question_patterns: Could you run the command sequence just provided, create a new archive, and tell me whether validation succeeds?
Please try those commands in order and report what happens when you archive and validate the app.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: This option works for me. I ran flutter clean and flutter build ios --config-only before archiving, and validation succeeded. I did not run flutter run before creating the archive.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I followed the command sequence, but validation still fails with the same error.
The sequence works, but I also ran pod install before opening Xcode.

edges.comment: Reporter c18, c25, and c72: the reporter described and later explicitly confirmed the workaround. This is modeled as a measurement clarification because the handler asks the reporter to test a procedure and report the raw outcome.

solution.intent: Fix Flutter's iOS native-assets embedding so a device archive receives only the native frameworks required by its current manifest, rather than stale simulator frameworks left in the shared native-assets directory; until using a fixed Flutter toolchain, create a clean config-only build immediately before archiving and do not run a simulator build first.
solution.concrete_example: For the affected sqlite3-based project, clean the build, fetch packages, prepare the iOS configuration, and archive directly in Xcode without first running a simulator build. The Flutter tooling fix should copy only the native frameworks selected for the current device target instead of every framework left under build/native_assets/ios.
solution.inference_hint: Maintainers reproduced that building for a simulator could leave sqlite3arm64ios_sim.framework under build/native_assets/ios and that the iOS embedding step copied the whole directory into a later device archive. Determining that Flutter must filter assets according to the current native-assets manifest was engineer-side analysis in c15-c21; the reporter supplied dependencies, validation results, and successful workaround behavior, not that implementation diagnosis.

edges.comment: The original reporter's chain is the native-assets issue established in c15-c21 and summarized separately as Issue 1 in c71. The initial claim that the sqlite3 package itself was responsible was corrected by participant5: Flutter creates and embeds these frameworks. The separate all-iOS-apps regression discussed from c62 onward is deliberately not spliced into this reporter's dependency-specific chain. The reporter confirmed the workaround in c72 but did not report testing the shipped tooling fix on their own project.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause for the reporter's project: Flutter's iOS native-assets embedding copied a stale sqlite3 simulator framework into a device archive instead of limiting embedded frameworks to the current target's native-assets manifest.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the sqlite-related dependencies, failure during Xcode Validate App, the simulator-before-archive reproduction, and the reporter's successful clean pre-archive workaround.

Must attribute the embedding mistake to Flutter tooling rather than dismissing it as a sqlite3 plugin bug; the package emits target-specific assets, while Flutter performs the erroneous copy into the archive.
Must not claim that merely updating to Flutter 3.38.2 and running flutter clean resolves the issue, because the reporter tried that and the same validation error remained.

A temporary workaround may clean and prepare the iOS configuration immediately before archiving while avoiding a simulator run first; the durable fix must filter native assets for the current device target.

Must ask the reporter to verify an archive built with the fixed Flutter tooling before claiming that the shipped SDK fix itself is confirmed; only the workaround was explicitly verified by the reporter.

persona_hint.experience_level: Experienced Flutter application developer who can share full dependency files, run Flutter and CocoaPods commands, inspect Xcode archive behavior, and test alternate build sequences, but relies on maintainers for Flutter-tool internals.
persona_hint.communication_style: Cooperative and conversational; provides requested files and exact errors, asks practical questions about Xcode behavior, and clearly reports when proposed updates or workarounds do and do not work.
